intent.name: suspension.recommend
intent.summary: Recommend a suspension from a recorded incident, with the reason and the days proposed. Coordinator, one step, and it excludes nobody yet.

routesHere.gloss: recommend a three-day suspension for this incident

request.gloss: remove the child from the school

routesElsewhere.note: A suspended student is not withdrawn. The place is held and the enrolment continues (BR-5, BR-8).

request.text: aaj hi ghar bhej do
request.gloss: send them home today

routesElsewhere.note: The Principal approves the suspension and sets the start date. Nothing excludes a child before that (BR-2).

request.text: sirf waqiya darj karo
request.gloss: just record the incident

routesElsewhere.note: A suspension is raised from an incident already recorded — a sanction with no recorded incident behind it cannot be defended (BR-1, E1).

steps.note: One step. It is a recommendation — the Principal approves it and sets the dates, and this approval is not configurable to a lower role (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A recommendation with no incident, and one with zero or fewer days, are both refused.
plan.atomicity: One write: the recommendation and the audit entry together or not at all. **Nothing changes for the student.** They attend as normal until the Principal approves it and the start date arrives. A suspension is never deleted, and a recommendation that was returned or refused stays on the record (BR-12).

planningRules.rule: Never create or infer the incident. The suspension is raised from one already recorded (BR-1, E1), and a sanction resting on an incident a planner described is a sanction with nothing behind it.
Never compose the reason. It is what the family is told and what the record carries (BR-1, BR-4), and it is read back if the sanction is questioned.
Never choose the number of days. It is what the Coordinator recommends, and the Principal sets the actual dates — a figure a planner supplied is days of a child's schooling.
Report an open support record. Where the student has one it is reviewed before approval, because behaviour is sometimes a symptom of something the school already knows about (BR-3, E5).
Report earlier suspensions. Repeated ones are visible together because a pattern is what leads to an expulsion (BR-11) — how many constitute that pattern is not decided anywhere in this use case.
Say plainly that nothing changes yet. The student attends as normal until the Principal approves it and the start date arrives (BR-2).

steps.note: One step, and it reaches attendance and the family. The Principal approves and sets the dates, and this approval is not configurable to a lower role (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An unreviewed open support record, a return date before the start, and an approval by anybody below the Principal are all refused.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the suspended state across the period, the attendance coded suspended rather than absent, and the notification to the guardian together or not at all. operations.name: suspension.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: suspension_id, since a suspension is approved once and a repeat must not notify the family twice
operations.purpose: Approve the suspension, setting its dates and terms.

parameters.name: suspension_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No suspension matches for that student at a state that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with the student, the incident, the proposed days and the status.

parameters.notes: The suspension, resolved from the student and its state.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.notes: When the exclusion begins. Set by the Principal at approval (BR-2).

parameters.name: return_date
parameters.notes: When the student returns. On or after the start date (E6). The state reverts by itself on it (BR-9).

parameters.name: may_sit_examination
parameters.notes: Whether the student may sit an examination falling within the period. Decided at approval and recorded (BR-7). Where they do not sit, the paper is recorded as an exam absence and classified there.

parameters.name: conditions_of_return
parameters.notes: What is required before the student returns. The family is told it with the dates (BR-4) — a condition a planner wrote is the school requiring something nobody decided.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: return_date
fields.description: When the state reverts by itself (BR-9).

fields.name: examinations_in_period
fields.description: Papers falling within the period. Where the student does not sit, each is recorded as an exam absence and classified there (BR-7).

fields.name: attendance_coded
fields.description: Suspended, not absent. No absence alert is sent and the days are not counted as unexplained absence (BR-6).

fields.name: place_held
fields.description: True. On the roster, in class counts, and invoiced as normal (BR-5).

fields.name: guardian_notified
fields.description: Delivery status. Where the guardian cannot be reached the suspension stands and the failure is reported (E9).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the dates. They are days a child is excluded from school, set by the Principal at approval (BR-2) — the recommended number of days is a recommendation, not the dates.
Never write the conditions of return. The family is told them and has to meet them (BR-4), and a condition a planner composed is the school requiring something nobody decided.
Never decide whether an examination may be sat. It is settled at approval and recorded (BR-7), and a paper missed is recorded as an exam absence with consequences for the result.
Never approve below the Principal. E3 and E4 are BR-2 working, and the Super Admin configures the permission but cannot set it below the Principal.

Report that the place is held. The student stays on the roster, in class counts and invoiced (BR-5) — the school is holding a place it is not letting the child occupy, and the family is still paying for it.
Report that attendance is coded suspended rather than absent. Without that state the guardian is alerted daily that their child did not arrive, at a school that sent them home (BR-6, E7).
Report a failed notification. The suspension stands, but a family that does not know the dates or the conditions cannot meet them (BR-4, E9).
